clue.text: Woman gets into trouble giving one warning of impending death

indicators.note: the woman word is placed so that it goes inside the trouble word

parts.note: a bane is a source of trouble or ruin
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman lands herself in difficulty while sounding an alarm about someone dying.
explanation.walkthrough: In Irish folklore this spirit wails to foretell a death in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish legend this female spirit wails outside a house to foretell that someone there will soon die.

clue.text: Silk used in a suit

parts.note: reads like fabric for tailoring, but a silk is a senior British lawyer (a QC or KC) who is employed in a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Fine fabric is chosen for a tailored outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a senior barrister is called a silk, from the silk gown worn on appointment as King's Counsel; a suit here is a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior courtroom advocates are nicknamed silks, and such a lawyer is engaged to argue a lawsuit.

clue.text: Curious thing that's worn by a woman in retirement

definitions.text: worn by a woman in retirement

indicators.note: curious means strange or odd, so the letters of thing are put into an odd new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Something odd is worn by a lady who has given up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' rearranges THING into NIGHT. Retirement here is going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A short nightdress is what a woman puts on when she retires to bed for the night.

clue.text: Male supporter defending English opener from now on

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a male

indicators.note: the supporter surrounds and so guards the English opener

parts.note: a rafter is a beam supporting a roof

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word English is taken

explanation.surface: A man who backs a team shields an English opening batsman from now on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like cricket talk for a batsman, but it only picks the first letter of English.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in future, at all times after the present moment.

clue.text: Hangman's execution appears to make a deep impression

indicators.note: an execution by beheading takes off the head, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Jack Ketch was a notorious seventeenth-century English hangman

explanation.surface: The way a hangman carries out a sentence seems to leave a deep mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch, hangman under Charles II, became a byword for the executioner. 'execution', read as beheading, removes his first letter K.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave a design deeply into metal or glass with acid is to cut a lasting mark into it.

clue.text: Ruler with Ganymede as a satellite?

definitions.meaning: the king of the Roman gods, ruler of the heavens
the largest planet, orbited by a moon called Ganymede

explanation.surface: A monarch keeps a beautiful youth as his hanger-on.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth Ganymede was also cupbearer to the chief god, which knits the two senses into one picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief Roman deity reigned over the gods, and the giant planet bearing his name has Ganymede among its moons.

clue.text: Having temporary mast is good reason for postponing the trial!

definitions.meaning: a ship fitted with a makeshift mast after damage is rigged in this improvised way

definitions.text: good reason for postponing the trial!
definitions.meaning: a panel of jurors that has been tampered with would force a court case to be put off

explanation.surface: A ship with a stopgap mast gives the court an excuse to delay proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvised sailing rig is a makeshift arrangement, and a fixed panel of jurors would wreck a fair hearing.

clue.text: Simple student in distress

indicators.note: the student letter is placed inside the distress word

parts.note: pain is distress or suffering
L is the learner plate on a British car, hence a student

explanation.surface: A straightforward learner is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain is unadorned and easy to understand, without complication.

clue.text: Something fishy about one's safari ending in this country

indicators.note: the fish surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: tuna is a fish
one is I, and the 's gives S

indicators.note: the last letter of the word safari is taken

explanation.surface: Something suspicious surrounds a holiday safari's finish in a North African land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something fishy' suggests suspicion, but it is a literal fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The North African republic is a sovereign state on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Note about textile fibre

parts.note: ray (or re) is the second note of the sol-fa scale
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A musical note concerning cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic fibre made from cellulose, used to weave fabric that resembles silk.

clue.text: Backing given to one man or another

definitions.meaning: radio speak for message received and agreed, a sign of assent
a common male first name, standing for any man

explanation.surface: Support offered to one fellow or some other.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio acknowledgement signals agreement, and it is also a familiar male forename.

clue.text: Defect in church transport? Sure thing!

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the defect word goes inside the transport abbreviation

parts.note: RY is short for railway
a taint is a flaw or blemish

explanation.surface: A fault in the vicar's car is guaranteed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church transport' reads as one phrase, but it splits into the church abbreviation and the railway one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bound to happen, beyond any doubt, is a dead cert.

clue.text: Popular feature, some say, of outstanding work here

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: signals that the word is pronounced, here in the British way that drops the final T

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature

explanation.surface: A well-liked characteristic is said to belong to some exceptional piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'trait' is often pronounced to rhyme with 'tray'. 'outstanding' means still to be done, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An office basket holds papers awaiting attention, unfinished business still to be dealt with.

clue.text: One related to a king, etc nothing less

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: less means minus, so the nothing letter is removed

parts.note: etc stands for 'and so on'
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone connected to royalty, and so forth, without anything extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' takes an O (nothing) from AND SO ON, giving ANDSON.
explanation.definitionFit: A son's son or daughter's son is a family member, a descendant two generations down.

clue.text: Sounds real bad, being falsely defamatory

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something seems really awful when it unfairly damages a reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges SOUNDSREAL. 'Sounds' tempts a homophone, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken statements that untruthfully damage someone's good name are actionable as slander.

clue.text: Illegal acquisition of keys in odd parts of Tahiti

indicators.note: the keys go inside the selected letters
the first, third and fifth letters of the word Tahiti are taken

parts.note: E and F are musical keys

explanation.surface: Unlawfully getting hold of keys on a strange Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: Musical keys are named by letters A to G, so 'keys' can supply any two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is taking property unlawfully, a criminal way of acquiring goods.

clue.text: Many a Roman youth initially in the army

parts.note: legion means a great number, many

indicators.note: the opening letters of the words Roman and youth are taken

explanation.surface: Plenty of young Romans are first of all soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes RY from Roman youth. The definition reads as an adjective phrase: one serving in a legion.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a unit of the Roman military, so a member of it served as a soldier.

clue.text: Orders binding Flanagan, an island investigator

indicators.note: the orders wrap round the comedian's name

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, so OMS are orders
Bud Flanagan was a British comedian of Flanagan and Allen
Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Instructions tie up a comedian, an islander checking complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: Bud Flanagan was a mid-century British music-hall comic, half of the double act Flanagan and Allen.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who looks into complaints against public bodies examines grievances for citizens.

clue.text: Settle here or shirk involvement in the old environment

indicators.note: the old word forms the surroundings for the jumbled letters

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

indicators.note: involvement suggests things twisted or tangled together, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Make your home here or avoid joining in the old surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a market town in the north of England, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Settle is a small town in the Dales, located in this northern English county.

clue.text: "And none so poor to do him — " (J. Caesar )

definitions.text: "And none so poor to do him — " (J. Caesar )

parts.words: "And none so poor to do him — " (J. Caesar )
parts.note: a line from Mark Antony's funeral speech in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar with its last word missing, a word for deep respect

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's Roman tragedy with a word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Antony laments that the dead Caesar, once mighty, now lies with none so poor to do him honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means deep respect or homage, which no one now pays the fallen Caesar.

clue.text: Long-serving surgeon has near disaster

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruin, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal doctor has a narrow escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges NEAR into ERAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with many years of service in a role is an old hand, experienced.

clue.text: Sounds like one removing water from agricultural machinery

indicators.note: the words point to a spoken match

parts.note: a bailer scoops water out of a boat

explanation.surface: Someone scooping water seems to be part of the farm kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm machine that compresses hay or straw into bundles is a piece of agricultural equipment.

clue.text: A match for the morning star

definitions.meaning: an old name for a friction match struck to make fire
Venus seen before dawn, also a name of Satan in tradition

explanation.surface: An equal partner for the dawn planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Early friction matches bore this name, and the light-bringer of Latin was Venus at dawn.

clue.text: Man carrying animal walked unsteadily

indicators.note: the man holds the animal inside him

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
an otter is an animal

explanation.surface: A fellow lugging a beast staggered along.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted is a short form of Edward, a stock crossword man.
explanation.definitionFit: To move on shaky legs, swaying as if about to fall, is to stagger.

clue.text: A sign leading to Kenya

indicators.note: leading points to the front part of the words to Kenya, where the letters lie

explanation.surface: A signpost points the way to an East African country.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the opening run of 'to Kenya'.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a symbol or indication, something standing for something else.

clue.text: Stand to drop a pound

parts.note: to ease is to lessen or let fall
L is the symbol for a pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: Prices are steady before falling by a quid.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's frame for holding a canvas upright is a stand.

clue.text: Orders set out to protect detectives in retrospect

indicators.note: the jumbled letters surround and shield the detectives
out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
looking back means the detectives' letters are read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: Instructions are laid out to guard police officers, as it turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police detective branch; 'in retrospect' means looking back, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrees issued by an authority are official commands.

clue.text: Lover's knot, say

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken

parts.note: a bow is a knot with loops

explanation.surface: A true-lover's knot, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover's' is 'Lover is', so 'Lover' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer or boyfriend courting a woman is her sweetheart.

clue.text: Broke nets when manoeuvring by the side of the road

definitions.text: by the side of the road
definitions.note: a phrase for a thing found there, standing for the noun

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving around, so the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Damaged netting being shifted beside the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges BROKENETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Edging blocks run along the margin of a pavement next to the carriageway.

clue.text: Muslim legal expert in plain clothes

definitions.meaning: an Islamic scholar who gives rulings on religious law
civilian dress worn by someone usually in uniform

explanation.surface: An Islamic jurist turns up out of uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: An Islamic jurisconsult issues fatwas, and the same word is military slang for civvies.

clue.text: Perplexity no advantage in a note — quite the opposite

indicators.note: this flips the word in round, so the advantage phrase holds the note rather than the reverse

parts.note: no plus means no advantage

explanation.surface: Confusion at having no edge in a musical passage, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a note' would put the phrase inside the note; 'quite the opposite' says the note goes inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means bewilderment, a state of being baffled.

clue.text: Remove bottle from one in Paris? Cheek!

parts.note: un is French for one
nerve means cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: Taking courage away from a Parisian, how impudent!
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain someone of courage is to rattle them and weaken their resolve.
